Do not memorize a long list of shops.

Memorize this contrast:

many normal facilities → but nothing unique → I only go for specific reasons → every visit feels similar → convenient, not exciting

That contrast is the heart of the story.

11. Details to confirm later

Only add these if they are true and easy to remember:

  1. Approximately how far the mall is from your home.
  2. How often you go there.
  3. One specific movie you watched there.
  4. One promotional activity or event you remember.
  5. One thing you wish the mall would add to make it more interesting.

Core Story 007 — My Smartphone: Expensive but Essential

Why this is a core story

This is one real object that can naturally cover both:

  • OB10 — An item on which you spent more than expected
  • OB15 — Something you cannot live without

The facts stay mostly the same. Only the spotlight changes:

  • OB10: focus on the purchase, budget, and why the final cost was higher than expected.
  • OB15: focus on how often you use the phone and why it has become essential in daily life.

The central chain is:

needed a smartphone → expected to spend less → final cost was higher than planned → use it every day → communication + study + payment + navigation + information → expensive, but extremely useful

1. Basic background

  • The object is my smartphone.
  • I originally expected to spend less on it.
  • In the end, the total cost was higher than I had planned.
  • Even so, I use it every day and depend on it for many practical tasks.

2. Cue Card A — OB10: An item on which you spent more than expected

Best spotlight

Focus on:

planned budget → compared options → chose a more expensive model / configuration → extra cost → initial reaction → why I still think it was useful

Possible reasons the cost was higher

Only use the ones that are true:

  • I chose a model with more storage.
  • I wanted better performance or a better camera.
  • I bought accessories such as a case or charger.
  • I decided that paying more for a device I would use every day was reasonable.

A natural line:

I originally had a lower budget in mind, but I ended up spending more than I expected because I wanted a phone that would last longer and handle everything I use it for.

Feeling

A balanced answer works well:

At first, I felt a little uncomfortable about the price, but over time I felt the extra money was justified because I use the phone constantly.

3. Cue Card B — OB15: Something you cannot live without

Do not take “cannot live without” literally. In IELTS, you can explain that it is something you depend on heavily in everyday life.

What I use it for

  • contacting family and friends
  • studying and searching for information
  • using maps and navigation
  • making digital payments
  • taking photos
  • checking schedules or messages
  • accessing useful apps
  • dealing with small everyday tasks quickly

A natural line:

I wouldn't say I literally couldn't survive without it, but it has become such an important part of my daily routine that life would be much less convenient without it.

4. Why it is essential

Do not just list functions. Group them into two or three larger ideas.

Communication

It is the main way I keep in touch with my family and friends.

Study and information

I use it to search for information, practise English, read messages, and deal with study-related tasks.

Daily convenience

It also works as my map, camera, payment tool, and access point for many services.

5. Balanced reflection

This makes the answer sound more mature.

Possible idea:

I rely on my phone a lot, but I also think it is important not to become completely dependent on it. The phone is useful because it saves time and combines many tools in one device, but I still try not to use it when I need to concentrate.

6. Useful vocabulary

  • budget
  • cost more than expected
  • spend more than planned
  • worth the money
  • justify the cost
  • storage
  • performance
  • essential device
  • rely on
  • depend on
  • daily routine
  • digital payment
  • navigation
  • keep in touch
  • convenient
  • all-in-one device
  • practical
  • frequently used

7. Useful phrases from the phrase bank

Unexpected cost

Explain why

The main reason was that I wanted something that would last longer.

Daily dependence

I rely on it for a lot of everyday tasks.

Balanced conclusion

It was expensive, but considering how often I use it, I think it was worth the money.

8. One-minute preparation keywords

OB10 — expensive item

smartphone → lower budget → compared models → spent more → features / storage → initially worried → daily use → worth it

OB15 — cannot live without

smartphone → communication → study → maps → payments → camera → daily routine → convenience → balanced reflection

9. Memory rule

Do not memorize two separate answers.

Memorize this one chain:

bought smartphone → cost more than planned → use it constantly → communication + study + daily services → expensive but valuable

Then change the spotlight:

  • OB10: price and purchase decision
  • OB15: usefulness and daily reliance

10. Details to confirm later

Only add these when they are true and easy to remember:

  1. The phone model.
  2. Approximately how much you expected to spend.
  3. Approximately how much you actually spent.
  4. The main reason you chose the more expensive option.
  5. The three apps or functions you use most often.
  6. How long you have owned the phone.

Core Story 008 — Boston: From a NeRF Project at MIT to a Celtics Game

Why this is a core story

This Boston experience now has two concrete scenes and one clear reflection:

short summer project at MIT → use NeRF to reconstruct 3D models from video → reduce noise in the reconstructed models → watch the Celtics at TD Garden → hear the home crowd support the team → revise my view of Boston → reflect on balancing research and everyday life

It can answer a city question and a live-sports question without inventing a second trip. The NeRF branch may also support a technology or project question after the exact smoothing method and result are confirmed.

1. Background

  • I went to Boston for a short summer project at MIT.
  • The project involved using NeRF technology to turn video footage into three-dimensional models.
  • The reconstruction process produced visible noise or artifacts in the 3D models.
  • My responsibility was to smooth the reconstructed models and reduce those artifacts.
  • During the same stay, I watched an NBA game at TD Garden.

A concise non-technical explanation of the project:

It was a short computer-vision project in which we used NeRF to reconstruct three-dimensional models from video footage.

2. The NeRF project scene

Goal

  • Use video footage as the input.
  • Apply NeRF-related techniques to reconstruct a 3D model or scene.

Problem

  • The reconstructed models contained noise and visual artifacts.
  • These artifacts made the surfaces look less clean or realistic.

My responsibility

  • I was responsible for smoothing the reconstructed models.
  • The purpose was to reduce the visible noise and improve the quality of the final 3D result.

Natural IELTS wording:

My main responsibility was dealing with the noise in the reconstructed models. I worked on smoothing the surfaces and reducing visual artifacts so that the final result would look cleaner.

Do not name a specific smoothing algorithm until it is confirmed.

3. The Celtics game at TD Garden

  • I watched an NBA game in person at TD Garden.
  • The Boston Celtics played another NBA team, but I no longer remember the opponent.
  • The opponent's name is not necessary for the story and should not be guessed.
  • What impressed me most was the patience and support of the home crowd.
  • When the Celtics were attacking, the audience shouted words such as “Go, Celtics, go!”
  • When the team was defending, the crowd repeatedly shouted “Defense!” and created a very loud atmosphere.

The strongest scene:

The most memorable part was not the final score. It was hearing the whole crowd change its chant with the game: they cheered for the Celtics on offense and shouted “Defense!” when the other team had the ball.

4. Change in my view of Boston

Before

  • I mainly associated Boston with universities, researchers, and a serious academic atmosphere.

After the experience

  • The Celtics game showed me a much more energetic and community-oriented side of the city.
  • I began to see Boston as a place where academic life and ordinary leisure can exist together.
  • The contrast between the MIT project and TD Garden made the city especially memorable.

Personal reflection

This is a personal conclusion, not a universal claim about every researcher:

The experience made me realize that research does not have to occupy every part of a person's life. Having interests outside work may help people protect their mental health, remain creative, and return to research with new energy.

5. Cue-card coverage

PL06 — Your favorite city that you have visited

Strong route, provided Boston is genuinely the city I want to name as my favorite.

Focus on:

summer project at MIT → original academic impression → Celtics game at TD Garden → energetic crowd → broader view of Boston → research-life balance

EV07 — A live sports event you watched before

This route is now supported by enough real detail.

Focus on:

NBA game → TD Garden → Celtics → opponent forgotten → offense and defense chants → supportive crowd → changed impression of the city

Technology or project topic

The NeRF branch can support a technology project or challenging technical problem:

video input → NeRF reconstruction → noisy 3D model → responsible for smoothing and artifact reduction

Before using it for a full challenge question, confirm the method I used, whether I worked alone or with a team, and how much the final model improved.

Other possible future uses

  • a trip that changed my opinion of a place
  • an experience that combined study and leisure
  • a time I saw a lively crowd
  • something that changed my view of work-life balance

6. Useful vocabulary

NeRF project

  • a short summer project at MIT

  • reconstruct a three-dimensional model
  • computer vision
  • NeRF
  • visual noise
  • visual artifacts
  • smooth the reconstructed model
  • reduce artifacts
  • improve the reconstruction quality

Basketball and city atmosphere

  • the home crowd
  • on offense
  • on defense
  • chant loudly

7. Useful corrections

Say:

I took part in a short summer project at MIT.

Not:

It was a tiny project of summer in MIT.

Say:

We used NeRF to transform video footage into 3D models.

Say:

Not:

Say:

Not:

Say:

The experience changed my view of the city.

8. One-minute preparation keywords

PL06 — Boston version

summer → MIT → NeRF project → academic impression → TD Garden → Celtics crowd → energetic side → balance → memorable city

EV07 — Live game version

TD Garden → NBA → Celtics → opponent forgotten → home crowd → offense chant → “Defense!” → loud support → changed impression

9. Memory rule

Do not memorize three unrelated answers. Memorize this contrast:

Then attach the NeRF technical branch or the Celtics crowd branch according to the cue card.

notes.text: IELTS Speaking Part 2 Knowledge Bank Purpose: Collect flexible personal material before trying to produce a full two-minute answer. This is not a memorised-answer bank. It is a reusable story bank. Each story should contain enough real details to fit several cue cards. How to build each knowledge card For every Part 2 topic, collect: Story title Core change, event, person, place, object, or experience Background Cause or motivation Specific actions One memorable scene Results Feelings and reflection Useful vocabulary and phrases Other cue cards that can reuse the story One-minute preparation keywords Do not write a full script first. Build the raw material, organise it, and then practise speaking from keywords. Core Story 001 — From Waiting to Taking Initiative Why this is a core story This is one personal experience that can answer several different IELTS Part 2 cue cards. Do not memorize two separate answers. The central story is: I used to be more passive and wait for opportunities or help to come to me. Around the end of my third year of college, I started to believe that I should take more initiative. One concrete change was the way I studied: instead of relying mainly on memorization, classes, and teachers, I began using AI actively as a personal study assistant, especially for IELTS speaking practice. The facts stay mostly the same. Only the spotlight changes according to the cue card. Cue card A — Describe a change that you made recently You should say: what the change was what caused the change what you did for the change how you feel about the change Best spotlight for this cue card Focus mainly on the study-routine change. Before: I studied more passively, especially through vocabulary memorization, lectures, online courses, and material prepared by other people. Change: I began using AI actively as a learning assistant and added much more speaking practice. Cause: I needed a more efficient and personalized way to prepare for IELTS, and I had started to believe that I should take more initiative instead of waiting for the perfect learning environment. Action: I began having live English conversations, asking for explanations and corrections, building phrase and Part 2 story banks, and using AI to clarify difficult academic ideas. Result: My learning became more active, personalized, and efficient. Possible opening One important change I made recently was changing the way I study. I used to rely much more on passive learning, but now I try to take more initiative and use AI actively as a study partner. Cue card B — Describe a time when you changed an important opinion of yours You should say: when you changed your opinion what your original opinion was why you changed it how you felt about the experience Best spotlight for this cue card Focus mainly on the mindset change. When: Around the end of my third year of college. Old opinion: I believed that opportunities depended heavily on luck and coincidence, so I often waited for the right chance to appear. Turning point: I saw people around me actively create opportunities. One memorable example was a social-media video about a person working in AI who kept learning, applying to companies, and sending out his CV instead of simply waiting. New opinion: If I want something, I should at least try. Action can create choices that would not exist if I only waited. Concrete proof of the new mindset: I changed the way I studied. Instead of waiting for teachers, classes, or ideal conditions to solve my learning problems, I started using AI proactively and practising speaking more actively. Possible opening I used to believe that good opportunities would eventually come if I waited long enough, but around the end of my third year of college, I started to see things differently. 1. Core story timeline Stage 1 — Before I was relatively passive about both opportunities and learning. I thought luck and coincidence were very important. In study, I relied heavily on memorizing vocabulary, lectures, online courses, and explanations from teachers. I sometimes knew a word when reading it but could not retrieve it quickly while speaking. Because I can be shy about asking questions, I did not always get the personal explanations I needed in a large class. Stage 2 — Turning point Near the end of my third year of college, I started thinking more seriously about my future. I noticed that classmates and other people often had more choices because they tried more things. I watched a social-media video about someone working in artificial intelligence. He talked about continuing to learn, applying to many companies, and sending his CV out instead of waiting for the perfect opportunity. That example made the idea of taking initiative feel concrete rather than abstract. Stage 3 — New mindset I used to believe that opportunities mainly came from luck, but now I think action creates opportunities. Related ideas: Trying does not guarantee success, but not trying removes the possibility completely. Waiting can feel safe, but it can also make me passive. I should create more choices for myself instead of expecting choices to appear automatically. Stage 4 — Concrete behavior change: AI-assisted study This is the strongest proof that the opinion change affected your real behavior. I stopped treating study as only memorization and passive input. I began practising spoken English in live AI conversations. I ask for questions to be repeated, slowed down, or explained in simpler language. I ask for grammar and vocabulary corrections after I speak. I build a phrase bank and a reusable Part 2 core-story bank. I use AI to clarify university material when a lecture or textbook explanation is not enough. I use AI to reduce repetitive work and make study time more efficient. 2. Memorable scenes Scene A — Social-media turning point I remember watching a video in which someone working in AI explained that he kept sending his CV to different companies and continued trying even when opportunities did not appear immediately. Use this scene when the question is about: changing an opinion inspiration social media a person who influenced you persistence career choices Scene B — AI speaking practice During an IELTS speaking practice session, I did not understand a cue-card word, so I asked the AI to slow down and explain it. After I understood the meaning, I was able to continue the answer instead of simply giving up. Use this scene when the question is about: a recent change technology learning solving a problem communication becoming more independent 3. Results Practical results I can practise speaking more frequently. I receive feedback immediately. I have a more personalized study process. I can identify weak points instead of only repeating familiar material. I am training vocabulary retrieval, not only vocabulary recognition. I use study time more efficiently. Mindset results I am becoming more willing to take initiative. I am less likely to wait for the perfect condition before starting. I see action as a way to create possibilities. I feel more responsible for my own progress. 4. Feelings and reflection Some feelings have not been fully confirmed yet, so keep this section flexible and only use wording that feels true in the exam. Possible ideas: more motivated more independent more confident slightly nervous because taking action also means risking failure relieved because I no longer have to wait for perfect conditions more responsible for my own future Strong reflection Looking back, I realize that the biggest change was not simply using a new technology. It was becoming more proactive and taking greater responsibility for my own learning and opportunities. 5. Useful vocabulary Mindset and opportunities take initiative be proactive be passive create opportunities look for opportunities rely on luck coincidence turning point mindset step out of my comfort zone keep trying apply to a company send out a CV / résumé Learning and AI personalized learning active practice passive memorization immediate feedback retrieve vocabulary clarify a difficult concept identify weaknesses improve study efficiency learning assistant live conversation repetitive work Useful corrections Say: AI has developed rapidly. Not: AI grows fastly. Say: improve my study efficiency Not: improve my study quick Say: If I don't try, the opportunity may never appear. Not: If I not try, the choice will never be presented there. Say: speak with an AI assistant in real time or: have a live conversation with an AI assistant 6. Useful phrases from the phrase bank Old mindset I used to believe that good opportunities would simply appear if I waited long enough. Turning point What changed my mind was seeing other people actively create opportunities for themselves. Lesson That experience made me realize that opportunities usually require action. Link the mindset to the behavior change One concrete change I made was becoming much more active in the way I study. Instead of waiting for teachers or classes to solve every problem, I started using AI as a study partner. This was part of a bigger change in my mindset: I wanted to take more initiative instead of simply waiting. Observation One thing I've noticed is that I remember new words better when I use them in conversation. Gradual result Over time, I've become more confident speaking English and more willing to take initiative. Reflection Looking back, I realize that active learning suits me much better than passive memorization. 7. Reusable cue-card topics This single core story can be adapted for: a change you made recently a time you changed an important opinion a positive change in your life a piece of technology you find useful an app or tool you often use a new way of learning a skill you are learning something that improved your efficiency a time you solved a problem a difficult thing you learned a habit that helped you a piece of advice that influenced you a person who inspired you something interesting you saw on social media a video you remember a time you learned something important a decision that changed your behavior a time you became more confident or independent 8. How to change the spotlight If the cue card is about a recent change Spend most of the answer on: old study routine → new AI-assisted routine → specific actions → results Keep the mindset change as the reason behind it. If the cue card is about a changed opinion Spend most of the answer on: old belief → social-media/classmate turning point → new belief → AI study change as proof If the cue card is about technology Spend most of the answer on: AI tool → how you use it → specific speaking example → why it is useful If the cue card is about something seen on social media Spend most of the answer on: AI professional's video → CV/application detail → why it impressed you → how it changed your behavior If the cue card is about a person who inspired you Spend most of the answer on: the person's persistence → why it stood out → what you learned → what you changed afterward 9. One-minute preparation keywords For the recent-change cue card passive study → AI partner → IELTS → live speaking → feedback → more active → efficient → reflection For the changed-opinion cue card end of 3rd year → wait for chances → AI video → many CVs → take initiative → AI study change → more proactive 10. Memory rule Do not memorize two complete answers. Memorize this one cause-and-effect chain: passive mindset → turning point → take initiative → change study behavior → AI as concrete example → better results → reflection Then, during the exam, decide which part deserves the most time based on the cue card. 11. Details to confirm later To make the story even stronger and more personal, add these only when they are true and easy to remember: The approximate month when this mindset shift became clear. One exact real action outside studying that shows you took more initiative. Your genuine feeling immediately after making the change. One academic subject where AI gave you a particularly useful explanation. Core Story 002 — Building a Line-Following Car as a Team 1. Core idea During the last term, I worked in a four-person university team to build a small DIY car that could follow a line, use radar/sensors to detect obstacles, and move automatically. The project did not fully succeed, but it gives me a strong real story about teamwork, engineering, technical problems, imagination, time pressure, and learning from failure. 2. Background The project was part of a university course in the last term. The goal was to build a small autonomous car from scratch rather than simply copy an existing finished design. The car needed to follow a line and detect obstacles. There were four members in the team. 3. Team roles The work was divided among the four members: one member focused mainly on PID control; one member designed the driving circuit / PCB; one member was responsible for the lab notebook and final report; my main responsibility was to design and 3D-print the car structure and assemble the components. Useful simple IELTS version We divided the work according to different technical tasks, and my main responsibility was designing the car body, 3D-printing it, and assembling the components. 4. Main difficulty The team faced several connected problems. Circuit and PCB delay Designing and producing the circuit board took longer than expected. Because of that delay, there was very little time left for PID testing and tuning. Mechanical problem The physical structure of the car also caused problems. The distance between the bottom of the car and the floor was too small. At times, the car did not move as expected because parts of the structure were too close to the ground. Control problem The PID parameters could not simply stay fixed. The team needed more time to test and adjust them under different conditions. Because testing time was limited, the final performance was unstable. 5. Result The project did not fully succeed in the final test. The failure was not caused by one single mistake. It came from several factors: circuit delays, limited testing time, mechanical design problems, and insufficient PID tuning. This is useful for IELTS because the story does not need a perfect ending. The important part is explaining what happened and what I learned. 6. What I learned A technical project needs enough time for integration and testing, not only individual component design. Mechanical design, electronics, and control algorithms affect one another. A team can divide tasks, but members still need to communicate because one person's delay can affect everyone else's work. A failed result can still be valuable if I understand the causes and know what I would improve next time. Possible reflection Looking back, I realize that building each part separately was not enough. We also needed much more time to test how all the parts worked together. 7. Cue cards this story can cover Strong / already supported by the real experience EV09 — A time when you worked in a group Focus on: four members → different responsibilities → your 3D-printing and assembly role → technical problems → final result → teamwork lesson EV05 — A challenging technological problem you faced Focus on: DIY autonomous car → circuit delay → little testing time → mechanical/PID problems → attempted adjustments → what you learned EV14 — A time when you used imagination Focus on: no ready-made final design → designing the car structure → deciding how to arrange and assemble components → 3D printing → testing the physical design Potentially reusable, but more real details are needed first PE06 — A person who gave a clever solution to a problem This can use the same project only if one teammate genuinely proposed a specific clever solution that you remember. EV13 — A time when you encouraged someone to do something they didn't want to do Use this project only if you genuinely encouraged a teammate to take an action they were reluctant to take. PE10 — A person who makes plans a lot Use this project only if one real teammate was clearly the person who organised schedules, divided tasks, or made detailed plans. Additional confirmed use EV03 — A time when you received a message or email and it took you a long time to reply This project can support EV03 naturally. Around six days before the deadline, the team was under heavy time pressure and spent most of the day working on the car. Because I was so focused on the project, I barely checked my phone. Messages from my parents or friends sometimes stayed unread for much longer than usual, so I replied several hours later. Natural version: We were only about six days away from the deadline, so I was extremely busy with the project and barely had time to check my phone. As a result, I sometimes didn't see messages from my parents or friends until much later, and I replied several hours later than I normally would. Conditional use EV19 — An occasion when you were not allowed to use a mobile phone Use this project for EV19 only if there was a genuine rule or agreement restricting phone use during the work session, for example a lab rule or a real team agreement to put phones away. Simply being too busy to check the phone is not the same as being not allowed to use it. Do not invent these details just to increase coverage. 8. How to change the spotlight If the cue card is about teamwork Spend most of the answer on: team goal → division of work → your responsibility → coordination problem → outcome → teamwork lesson If the cue card is about a technological challenge Spend most of the answer on: what the car was supposed to do → PCB delay → limited PID testing → mechanical issue → why the test failed → technical lesson If the cue card is about imagination Spend most of the answer on: building something from scratch → designing the physical structure → 3D printing → arranging components → turning an idea into a real object If the cue card is about a late reply to a message Spend most of the answer on: six days before deadline → intense project work → barely checked phone → missed family/friend message → replied much later → explain/apologise If the cue card says you were not allowed to use your phone Only use this story if a real restriction existed. Focus on: actual rule/agreement → why phones were restricted → project work → missed message → later reply 9. Memory rule Do not memorize three separate answers. Memorize this one event chain: university project → four-person team → build DIY line-following car → divide roles → my 3D-printing/assembly task → circuit delay → limited testing → mechanical + PID problems → unsuccessful final test → lessons Optional communication branch for EV03: deadline pressure → barely checked phone → missed a message → replied much later Then change which part gets the most attention depending on the cue card. 11. Details to confirm later Only add these when they are real and easy for you to remember: The exact course or subject in which you did the project. Whether the sensor was specifically radar, ultrasonic, infrared, or another type. One specific moment when the team discovered the clearance problem. One specific adjustment you personally made to the structure. Whether one teammate proposed a clever solution that could support PE06. Whether one teammate was especially good at planning, which could support PE10. Your genuine feeling after the final test failed. Core Story 003 — Reconnecting with Friends at a Spider-Man Movie 1. Core idea After not seeing some friends for a long time, we arranged a movie outing because we are all Marvel fans. We chose a Spider-Man film, I booked the tickets, and the outing gave us a natural chance to reconnect and enjoy being together again. 2. Background We had not met for quite a long time. We are all interested in Marvel movies and comics. When a Spider-Man film came out, it gave us an easy reason to meet again. Because we already knew the characters and the Marvel universe well, we had plenty to talk about before and after the movie. 3. My role I helped turn the idea into an actual plan. I booked the movie tickets. The plan itself was simple, which made it easy for everyone to join. A natural sentence: Since we hadn't seen each other in ages, I suggested that we watch the new Spider-Man movie together and I booked the tickets. 4. Vivid details The strongest details are not complicated facts about the movie. They are the small interactions between friends. We talked about the characters because all of us were Marvel fans. After the movie, we discussed what we liked and how we would rate it. One friend thought it was the best of the three Spider-Man films starring Tom Holland. We also talked about future Marvel films we were looking forward to. The playful discussion made the outing feel more personal than simply sitting in a cinema. A useful line: We ended up talking about the movie for quite a while, and one of my friends even said it was his favourite of the three Tom Holland Spider-Man films. 5. Why I enjoyed the experience Do not stop at: It improved our friendship. Extend the idea in three layers: Reconnection We hadn't met for a long time, so the outing gave us a chance to reconnect. Feeling I felt relaxed and comfortable because I was spending time with people who shared the same interests. Small moment Our playful debate about the movie reminded me how much I had missed talking with them. A natural combined version: What made the experience special was that we hadn't seen each other in ages. Watching the movie gave us a reason to meet again, but the part I enjoyed most was actually the conversation afterward. We joked about the characters, compared our opinions, and I realized how much I had missed spending time with them. 6. Result and reflection The outing helped us reconnect after a long period without meeting. It reminded me that friendships need some active effort to maintain. A simple shared interest can be enough to bring people together again. The experience was memorable mainly because of the people, not because the activity itself was unusual. Possible reflection: Looking back, I realize that the movie was really just an excuse to meet. What mattered most was reconnecting with my friends. 7. Useful vocabulary reconnect with friends keep in touch share the same interests book the tickets arrange an outing have a lot to talk about debate something playfully catch up with someone spend quality time together strengthen a friendship a shared interest a memorable outing 8. Confirmed and conditional cue-card coverage Strongest confirmed uses This story is naturally useful for: a happy event or outing you helped organize a small gathering with friends, when the cue card does not require a birthday, cake, special food, or a large crowd an enjoyable experience with friends a time you reconnected with someone a memorable movie-going experience an activity you enjoyed because of the people you were with Conditional use in the current May–August topic bank EV01 — A happy event you organized: usable if you present the movie outing as the event you arranged and clearly explain your role in booking/planning it. OB11 — A movie you watched recently: usable only if the Spider-Man movie was genuinely recent enough for you to describe honestly. Gathering boundary The earlier conversation used this outing as the real example for a small gathering with friends. That is valid when the prompt only requires people to meet and enjoy an activity together. In that version, focus on: friends had not met for a long time → shared Marvel interest → arranged the outing → watched the movie → talked afterward → reconnected The word gathering does not automatically mean a birthday party. The same story stops being suitable when the cue card specifically requires details that did not happen. Do not force this story into EV10 — a special cake OB07 — food eaten during a special event EV12 — an occasion when many people were smiling, unless you have a real scene involving a larger group birthday or party questions that specifically require decorations, gifts, a cake, special food, or other details this outing did not actually contain This story therefore covers a general small gathering, but not every birthday or party topic. Keep it because it is authentic and easy to remember, while preserving the factual boundary above. 9. How to change the spotlight If the cue card is about organizing an event Focus on: long time without meeting → common Marvel interest → suggest movie → book tickets → everyone joins → enjoyable result If the cue card is about friendship Focus on: long gap → reconnect → shared interest → conversation after movie → feeling closer again If the cue card is about a movie Focus on: why you chose Spider-Man → Marvel background → reaction to the film → discussion with friends → personal opinion 10. One-minute preparation keywords Event / outing version long time no see → Marvel fans → Spider-Man → booked tickets → cinema → talked afterward → reconnect → friendship Friendship version old friends → hadn't met → shared interest → movie → debate → laugh/talk → missed them → reconnect Movie version Spider-Man → Marvel fan → friends → characters → Tom Holland trilogy → discussion → opinion → memorable 11. Memory rule Do not memorize a long movie review. Memorize this simple human chain: hadn't met for a long time → shared Marvel interest → Spider-Man gave us a reason to meet → I booked tickets → watched together → talked and debated afterward → reconnected → realized I had missed them The strongest part of this story is friendship and reconnection, not technical knowledge about Marvel. 12. Details to confirm later Only add these if they are true and easy to remember: Which exact Spider-Man film you watched. Approximately when the outing happened. How many friends went with you. Whether you suggested the movie first or only booked the tickets. One funny or memorable sentence from the discussion afterward. How long you had gone without seeing these friends. Core Story 004 — Ershou Lake: From a Polluted Lake to a Cleaner Public Place Why this is now a core story This story is stronger than the earlier backup version because it now has a clear before-and-after change, a real place, a family connection, an environmental-policy angle, and a future-policy opinion. The central chain is: Ershou Lake near my hometown → dirty and unpleasant in the past → local government introduced environmental measures and developed the area → the lake became cleaner and more attractive → more people started visiting → I now walk there with my family → I would support stricter anti-littering and ecosystem-protection rules Do not invent the official name of an existing law. At the moment, the confirmed fact is that local environmental measures or cleanup actions were introduced; the exact legal title has not been verified. 1. Background The lake is called Ershou Lake and is near my hometown. My grandparents used to go fishing there in the past. It was not a particularly famous place before. In the past, the lake was dirty and sometimes smelled unpleasant. Later, the local government introduced environmental cleanup or protection measures and developed the surrounding area for tourism. The area gradually became cleaner and more attractive to visitors. I now sometimes walk around the lake with my family. 2. The environmental change Before The lake looked less attractive. The water and surrounding environment were dirtier. There was an unpleasant smell. The area was not a major place for visitors. After Environmental cleanup and management improved the area. The lake became cleaner. Tourism and nearby commercial activity developed. More people began visiting the area. It became a more pleasant place for local families to walk and relax. A natural sentence: One thing I've noticed is that the whole area has changed a lot. It used to be quite dirty and unpleasant, but after the local government introduced environmental measures, it gradually became much cleaner and more attractive. 3. Personal connection This should not become only a general environmental-policy answer. Keep the story personal. My grandparents used to fish there. I now walk around the lake with my family. Walking there helps me relax and clear my mind. It gives me a chance to take my mind off study pressure. The change is easy for me to notice because I have a family connection with the place. Possible line: What makes the change meaningful to me is that the lake is close to my hometown and my grandparents used to fish there, so it is not just a tourist attraction to me. 4. Cue Card A — OB01: A law or regulation about environmental protection Safe angle Because the exact official name of the law or regulation has not been confirmed, do not invent one. The safest preparation is: local environmental regulations or government measures aimed at cleaning the lake and controlling pollution Focus on: old condition → environmental measures → cleaner lake → tourism/public benefit → why you support the policy Who benefits local residents families who use the area for walking and recreation visitors and tourists local businesses that depend on a cleaner environment fish and other parts of the lake ecosystem How I feel supportive pleased that the environment improved impressed by the visible change aware that enforcement still matters Possible reflection: Looking back, I realize that environmental rules can feel abstract until you see a place change in front of you. In this case, the improvement is very visible. 5. Cue Card B — OB09: A new law you would like to introduce in your country This is a future proposal, so keep it clearly separate from the existing cleanup measures. My proposed policy I would like stricter rules around lakes and public waterways, especially: fines for people who throw rubbish into the lake or leave litter nearby stronger protection for the local ecosystem limits or controls on fishing practices if they damage fish populations or the balance of the ecosystem A natural version: If I could introduce a new rule, I would make littering around lakes much more strictly controlled, with clear fines for people who throw rubbish into the water. I would also like stronger rules to protect fish and the wider ecosystem. Why I would introduce it Cleaning a lake once is not enough. The improved environment needs to be protected over time. More visitors can also create more rubbish and pressure on the ecosystem. Environmental protection works better when people know there are clear consequences for harmful behavior. 6. Reusable place-topic coverage This same real place can also potentially support: PL01 — An important river/lake PL02 — A place in your country that you would like to recommend to travelers PL04 — A place you would like to visit in your free time EV02 — A special day out that did not cost you much If the question is about an important lake Focus on: hometown connection → grandparents fishing → environmental change → current public value If the question is about recommending a place Focus on: cleaner environment → walking area → family atmosphere → tourism development → why visitors may enjoy it If the question is about free time Focus on: walking with family → calm atmosphere → clear my mind → take my mind off study pressure If the question is about a low-cost day out Use this only if the visit genuinely costs little or nothing. Focus on: nearby lake → walking → family time → little spending → relaxing result 7. Useful vocabulary environmental protection environmental measures pollution control clean up a lake improve water quality public space local ecosystem protect fish populations litter / littering fine people for littering stricter enforcement tourism development attract visitors local residents preserve the environment maintain the improvement 8. Useful phrases from the phrase bank Describe change One thing I've noticed is that the whole area has changed a lot. Add the government action The local government introduced environmental measures to improve the area. Explain personal benefit It helps me clear my mind. It gives me a chance to take my mind off study pressure. Add a future proposal If I could introduce a new rule, I would... Explain why enforcement matters Cleaning the area once is not enough; the improvement also needs to be maintained. 9. One-minute preparation keywords Existing environmental-policy version Ershou Lake → hometown → dirty / bad smell → government measures → cleaner → tourism → residents + ecosystem benefit → support New-law version cleaner lake now → more visitors → litter risk → fines → protect fish → ecosystem → long-term protection Place version hometown lake → grandparents fishing → changed a lot → family walk → relax → recommend 10. Memory rule Do not memorize separate full answers for environmental law, new law, and lake/place questions. Memorize this one chain: Ershou Lake → dirty and unpleasant before → environmental cleanup → cleaner and more popular → family connection → benefit to people and nature → future need for stricter protection Then change the spotlight: OB01: existing environmental measures and their benefits OB09: the stricter rules you would introduce PL01 / PL02 / PL04 / EV02: the lake as a real place and personal experience 11. Details to confirm later Only add these if they are true or verified: The exact official name of the existing environmental law, regulation, or cleanup program. Approximately when the major cleanup or redevelopment happened. Whether fishing is currently regulated at Ershou Lake. One specific visible feature added during the tourism development. One particular family visit that you remember clearly. Whether visiting the lake is completely free or involves any small cost. Core Story 005 — Helping My Sister Choose a University Why this is a core story This is a real family decision that can be reused for giving advice, helping a family member, feeling proud of a family member, and potentially working with a family member. The central chain is: sister finishes an important exam → grades limit the available choices → she also has preferences about majors → my mother and I research universities with her → compare universities and majors → narrow down the options → help her make a final choice → feel proud and relieved Do not memorize a full answer. Memorize the decision-making process. 1. Background This happened several years ago when my sister needed to choose a university. Her exam results were an important factor because they affected which universities she could realistically apply to. She also had her own preferences about what subject or major she wanted to study. My mother and I helped her research the available choices. 2. What we actually did We searched online for universities that matched her grades. We looked at the majors available at different universities. We compared several options instead of choosing the first one we found. We considered both practical limits and her own interests. We discussed the advantages and disadvantages together. Finally, we helped her narrow the list down and make a decision. A natural sentence: My mother and I helped my sister research different universities and compare the majors they offered, based on both her grades and what she was interested in. 3. Why this was real collaboration This was not only one person giving help. My sister had to explain what she wanted. My mother and I helped collect and compare information. We discussed the options together. The final choice was made through a shared decision-making process. This makes the story useful for a working-with-a-family-member question if that question appears in another speaking bank. Possible line: We worked on it together because each of us contributed something different: my sister knew what she wanted, while my mother and I helped her compare the realistic options. 4. Strong route — EV17: A time when you gave advice to others Best spotlight Focus on: sister needs to choose university → many options → research → compare majors and universities → give advice → final decision What the advice was The advice was not simply: “Choose this university.” It was more like: choose an option that matches both your academic results and your genuine interest in the subject. Possible line: I tried not to make the decision for her. Instead, I helped her compare the choices and encouraged her to think about both the university and the major. 5. Strong or conditional route — EV18: A time when you felt proud of a family member This route is strongest if the pride came from something your sister genuinely did during or after this process. Possible reasons for pride, only if true: she made a thoughtful decision instead of following other people blindly she took responsibility for an important life choice she was admitted to a university she was happy with she adapted well after starting university Current confirmed feeling: I felt proud after we finally made the decision together. Add one more concrete reason later so that the pride is clearly about your sister, not only about finishing the research task. 6. Family-help route This story can also support questions about helping a family member. Focus on: important decision → she needed information → we researched together → I explained or compared options → she became more confident about the choice Possible line: I wanted to help because choosing a university can affect several years of someone's life, so I felt it was worth spending time on the decision. 7. Useful vocabulary university application academic results grades major / field of study available options compare different universities narrow down the choices weigh the pros and cons make an informed decision give advice respect someone's preference realistic option make the final choice work through a decision together 8. Useful phrases from the phrase bank Explain comparison We looked at several options before making a decision. Explain balanced advice We tried to balance what was realistic with what she genuinely wanted. Explain collaboration We worked through the decision together. Explain pride I was proud of her because she took the decision seriously. 9. One-minute preparation keywords Advice version sister → grades → majors → online research → compare universities → pros/cons → advice → final choice Family-help version important decision → many choices → research → explain → narrow down → support → relief Proud-family-member version sister → difficult choice → thought carefully → final decision → responsibility → proud Work-with-family-member version mother + me + sister → shared goal → divide information → compare → discuss → decide together 10. Memory rule Memorize this one chain: sister choosing university → grades + preferred major → mother and I help research → compare options → discuss pros and cons → sister makes final choice → proud / relieved Change the spotlight depending on the question: advice: what you suggested and why help: what practical support you provided pride: what your sister did that made you proud working together: how each person contributed to the same goal 11. Details to confirm later Only add these if they are true and easy to remember: Which year this happened. Which major or subject your sister preferred. Approximately how many universities you compared. One specific disagreement or difficult choice during the process. Which university she eventually chose. The exact reason you felt proud of her after the decision. Core Story 006 — Renhe Xincheng: A Convenient but Boring Shopping Center Why this is a core story This is a real place near my home that can naturally cover both: PL05 — A boring place PL08 — A shopping mall The central idea is not that the shopping center has nothing in it. In fact, it has many normal facilities. The reason I find it boring is that the experience feels repetitive and not very innovative. The central chain is: shopping center near my home → clothes / coffee / food / cinema / promotions → I sometimes go with friends or family → every visit feels similar → nothing feels unique → convenient but boring 1. Basic background The shopping center is called Renhe Xincheng. It is near my home. It has common facilities such as: clothing shops coffee shops restaurants or food options a cinema It sometimes has promotional activities or small events. 2. What I usually do there With friends I mainly go there to watch movies. The cinema is probably the main reason I visit with friends. With family I sometimes go there with my parents. We may have coffee or spend a little time there. A natural sentence: I don't go there because I love shopping. Most of the time, I only go there to watch a movie with friends or have a coffee with my parents. 3. Why I find it boring The problem is not that there are no activities. The real problem is: the shops are very similar to those in many other malls the promotions feel repetitive there is not much that feels new or surprising most of the activities are things I could do in almost any shopping center after a short time, I feel there is nothing else I really want to explore A strong natural explanation: Even though there are quite a few things to do, I still find it boring because every visit feels almost the same. The shops, promotions, and activities are quite predictable, so there is rarely anything that makes me curious or excited. 4. What an interesting shopping center should be like This is a useful extension if you need more ideas. For me, an interesting shopping center should: have something distinctive offer activities that are hard to find elsewhere change its events or exhibitions regularly give people a reason to visit beyond basic shopping, coffee, or movies A natural line: Personally, I think a good shopping center should have something unique that makes people want to go there specifically, rather than offering the same things you can find everywhere else. 5. Cue Card A — PL05: A boring place Best spotlight Focus on: near my home → looks convenient → many ordinary facilities → I have visited many times → every visit feels repetitive → nothing unique → bored Useful structure Where it is Why you went there What you can do there Why you still find it boring What would make it more interesting Possible reflection Looking back, I think the place is useful rather than enjoyable. I go there when I need something specific, but I rarely go there just for fun. 6. Cue Card B — PL08: A shopping mall Best spotlight For the shopping-mall question, do not make the whole answer negative. Focus on: location → facilities → who you go with → what you usually do → your balanced opinion A balanced conclusion: It is convenient because it is close to my home and has most of the basic things I need, but I wouldn't call it exciting because there is not much that feels distinctive. 7. Useful vocabulary shopping center / shopping mall convenient repetitive predictable ordinary not very distinctive lack variety promotional activities cinema coffee shop clothing store explore unique experience innovative stand out offer something different feel the same every time 8. Useful phrases from the phrase bank Explain repetition Every visit feels almost the same. Explain the lack of uniqueness There is nothing particularly unique about it. Explain limited motivation I usually go there only when I have a specific reason. Give a balanced opinion It is convenient, but I wouldn't call it exciting. 9. One-minute preparation keywords Boring-place version near home → Renhe Xincheng → clothes / coffee / food / cinema → many visits → same experience → predictable → nothing unique → boring Shopping-mall version location → facilities → friends / family → movies / coffee → convenient → repetitive → balanced opinion 10. Memory rule Do not memorize a long list of shops. Memorize this contrast: many normal facilities → but nothing unique → I only go for specific reasons → every visit feels similar → convenient, not exciting That contrast is the heart of the story. 11. Details to confirm later Only add these if they are true and easy to remember: Approximately how far the mall is from your home. How often you go there. One specific movie you watched there. One promotional activity or event you remember. One thing you wish the mall would add to make it more interesting. Core Story 007 — My Smartphone: Expensive but Essential Why this is a core story This is one real object that can naturally cover both: OB10 — An item on which you spent more than expected OB15 — Something you cannot live without The facts stay mostly the same. Only the spotlight changes: OB10: focus on the purchase, budget, and why the final cost was higher than expected. OB15: focus on how often you use the phone and why it has become essential in daily life. The central chain is: needed a smartphone → expected to spend less → final cost was higher than planned → use it every day → communication + study + payment + navigation + information → expensive, but extremely useful 1. Basic background The object is my smartphone. I originally expected to spend less on it. In the end, the total cost was higher than I had planned. Even so, I use it every day and depend on it for many practical tasks. 2. Cue Card A — OB10: An item on which you spent more than expected Best spotlight Focus on: planned budget → compared options → chose a more expensive model / configuration → extra cost → initial reaction → why I still think it was useful Possible reasons the cost was higher Only use the ones that are true: I chose a model with more storage. I wanted better performance or a better camera. I bought accessories such as a case or charger. I decided that paying more for a device I would use every day was reasonable. A natural line: I originally had a lower budget in mind, but I ended up spending more than I expected because I wanted a phone that would last longer and handle everything I use it for. Feeling A balanced answer works well: At first, I felt a little uncomfortable about the price, but over time I felt the extra money was justified because I use the phone constantly. 3. Cue Card B — OB15: Something you cannot live without Do not take “cannot live without” literally. In IELTS, you can explain that it is something you depend on heavily in everyday life. What I use it for contacting family and friends studying and searching for information using maps and navigation making digital payments taking photos checking schedules or messages accessing useful apps dealing with small everyday tasks quickly A natural line: I wouldn't say I literally couldn't survive without it, but it has become such an important part of my daily routine that life would be much less convenient without it. 4. Why it is essential Do not just list functions. Group them into two or three larger ideas. Communication It is the main way I keep in touch with my family and friends. Study and information I use it to search for information, practise English, read messages, and deal with study-related tasks. Daily convenience It also works as my map, camera, payment tool, and access point for many services. 5. Balanced reflection This makes the answer sound more mature. Possible idea: I rely on my phone a lot, but I also think it is important not to become completely dependent on it. The phone is useful because it saves time and combines many tools in one device, but I still try not to use it when I need to concentrate. 6. Useful vocabulary budget cost more than expected spend more than planned worth the money justify the cost storage performance essential device rely on depend on daily routine digital payment navigation keep in touch convenient all-in-one device practical frequently used 7. Useful phrases from the phrase bank Unexpected cost I ended up spending more than I expected. Explain why The main reason was that I wanted something that would last longer. Daily dependence I rely on it for a lot of everyday tasks. Balanced conclusion It was expensive, but considering how often I use it, I think it was worth the money. 8. One-minute preparation keywords OB10 — expensive item smartphone → lower budget → compared models → spent more → features / storage → initially worried → daily use → worth it OB15 — cannot live without smartphone → communication → study → maps → payments → camera → daily routine → convenience → balanced reflection 9. Memory rule Do not memorize two separate answers. Memorize this one chain: bought smartphone → cost more than planned → use it constantly → communication + study + daily services → expensive but valuable Then change the spotlight: OB10: price and purchase decision OB15: usefulness and daily reliance 10. Details to confirm later Only add these when they are true and easy to remember: The phone model. Approximately how much you expected to spend. Approximately how much you actually spent. The main reason you chose the more expensive option. The three apps or functions you use most often. How long you have owned the phone. Core Story 008 — Boston: From a NeRF Project at MIT to a Celtics Game Why this is a core story This Boston experience now has two concrete scenes and one clear reflection: short summer project at MIT → use NeRF to reconstruct 3D models from video → reduce noise in the reconstructed models → watch the Celtics at TD Garden → hear the home crowd support the team → revise my view of Boston → reflect on balancing research and everyday life It can answer a city question and a live-sports question without inventing a second trip. The NeRF branch may also support a technology or project question after the exact smoothing method and result are confirmed. 1. Background I went to Boston for a short summer project at MIT. The project involved using NeRF technology to turn video footage into three-dimensional models. The reconstruction process produced visible noise or artifacts in the 3D models. My responsibility was to smooth the reconstructed models and reduce those artifacts. During the same stay, I watched an NBA game at TD Garden. A concise non-technical explanation of the project: It was a short computer-vision project in which we used NeRF to reconstruct three-dimensional models from video footage. 2. The NeRF project scene Goal Use video footage as the input. Apply NeRF-related techniques to reconstruct a 3D model or scene. Problem The reconstructed models contained noise and visual artifacts. These artifacts made the surfaces look less clean or realistic. My responsibility I was responsible for smoothing the reconstructed models. The purpose was to reduce the visible noise and improve the quality of the final 3D result. Natural IELTS wording: My main responsibility was dealing with the noise in the reconstructed models. I worked on smoothing the surfaces and reducing visual artifacts so that the final result would look cleaner. Do not name a specific smoothing algorithm until it is confirmed. 3. The Celtics game at TD Garden I watched an NBA game in person at TD Garden. The Boston Celtics played another NBA team, but I no longer remember the opponent. The opponent's name is not necessary for the story and should not be guessed. What impressed me most was the patience and support of the home crowd. When the Celtics were attacking, the audience shouted words such as “Go, Celtics, go!” When the team was defending, the crowd repeatedly shouted “Defense!” and created a very loud atmosphere. The strongest scene: The most memorable part was not the final score. It was hearing the whole crowd change its chant with the game: they cheered for the Celtics on offense and shouted “Defense!” when the other team had the ball. 4. Change in my view of Boston Before I mainly associated Boston with universities, researchers, and a serious academic atmosphere. After the experience The Celtics game showed me a much more energetic and community-oriented side of the city. I began to see Boston as a place where academic life and ordinary leisure can exist together. The contrast between the MIT project and TD Garden made the city especially memorable. Personal reflection This is a personal conclusion, not a universal claim about every researcher: The experience made me realize that research does not have to occupy every part of a person's life. Having interests outside work may help people protect their mental health, remain creative, and return to research with new energy. 5. Cue-card coverage PL06 — Your favorite city that you have visited Strong route, provided Boston is genuinely the city I want to name as my favorite. Focus on: summer project at MIT → original academic impression → Celtics game at TD Garden → energetic crowd → broader view of Boston → research-life balance EV07 — A live sports event you watched before This route is now supported by enough real detail. Focus on: NBA game → TD Garden → Celtics → opponent forgotten → offense and defense chants → supportive crowd → changed impression of the city Technology or project topic The NeRF branch can support a technology project or challenging technical problem: video input → NeRF reconstruction → noisy 3D model → responsible for smoothing and artifact reduction Before using it for a full challenge question, confirm the method I used, whether I worked alone or with a team, and how much the final model improved. Other possible future uses a trip that changed my opinion of a place an experience that combined study and leisure a time I saw a lively crowd something that changed my view of work-life balance 6. Useful vocabulary NeRF project a short summer project at MIT video footage reconstruct a three-dimensional model computer vision NeRF visual noise visual artifacts smooth the reconstructed model reduce artifacts improve the reconstruction quality Basketball and city atmosphere an NBA game TD Garden the Boston Celtics the opposing team the home crowd on offense on defense chant loudly support the team an energetic atmosphere an academic atmosphere balance research with everyday life mental well-being 7. Useful corrections Say: I took part in a short summer project at MIT. Not: It was a tiny project of summer in MIT. Say: We used NeRF to transform video footage into 3D models. Say: The reconstructed models contained a lot of noise and visual artifacts. Not: There were many noise on the 3D models. Say: I was responsible for smoothing the models and reducing the artifacts. Say: I watched an NBA game at TD Garden. Not: I watched a basketball match near the basketball court. Say: I used to think Boston was mainly an academic city. The experience changed my view of the city. 8. One-minute preparation keywords PL06 — Boston version summer → MIT → NeRF project → academic impression → TD Garden → Celtics crowd → energetic side → balance → memorable city EV07 — Live game version TD Garden → NBA → Celtics → opponent forgotten → home crowd → offense chant → “Defense!” → loud support → changed impression Technology version video → NeRF → 3D reconstruction → noise/artifacts → my responsibility → smoothing → cleaner model → result? 9. Memory rule Do not memorize three unrelated answers. Memorize this contrast: MIT showed me Boston's academic side → TD Garden showed me its energetic everyday side → together they changed my understanding of the city Then attach the NeRF technical branch or the Celtics crowd branch according to the cue card. 10. Details to confirm later The approximate year and duration of the MIT summer project. Whether Boston is genuinely the favorite city I want to use for PL06. Who attended the Celtics game with me. Whether I remember the final result or one specific play; neither is required if I do not. The smoothing method or tool I used on the NeRF output. Whether the project was individual or team-based. How well the smoothing worked and how I felt about the final result. Verified Micro-materials from the Conversation Review These materials are real but currently too small for a full Core Story. Keep them as compact fact cards rather than padding them with invented events. Micro-material A — Walking after dinner Confirmed facts I usually take a walk around my home after dinner. I associate the habit with digestion, relaxation, and better sleep. The walk also gives me time to review what happened during the day and clear my mind. Potential uses a healthy habit an activity that helps me relax something I do after a busy day a simple way to improve well-being Details still needed for a full story the usual route and duration; whether I walk alone or with someone; one specific occasion or noticeable change caused by the habit. Micro-material B — Spicy food from my hometown Confirmed facts My hometown is known for spicy food. When I return, I like trying local specialties. Examples mentioned in the conversation include spicy hotpot and spicy fish. Potential uses food from my hometown a local specialty I would recommend something I like doing when I return home local culture or a hometown description Factual boundary This material does not currently cover OB07, food eaten during a special event. Returning home and eating local food is not automatically a special event. Details still needed for a full story the hometown's name, if I want to use it; one specific restaurant, family meal, or visit; which dish I prefer and why; one sensory detail and my genuine reaction. Blank Core Story Template Core Story ___ — [Story title] Primary cue card [Paste the cue card here.] Core idea [One or two sentences.] Background Cause or motivation What I did Memorable scene [Describe one real moment.] Results Feelings and reflection Useful vocabulary Useful phrases Reusable cue cards One-minute preparation keywords keyword → keyword → keyword → keyword → result → lesson
